source_read: PDF PDFs/Ketamine/Malhotra_1996_NMDAHumanCognition.pdf, printed pp. 301-307 (all 7 pages). Scanned pages with an error-prone text layer: every number used was checked on pages rendered at 150 dpi (Results p. 303, Table 1 and Results/Figure 2 p. 304, Methods p. 302); Figure 1 values read from the plot and labelled as such.

claims.overstatement: Two wording points. (1) '13 of 15 people recalled less and 9 of 15 scored lower on the attention measure' names no comparison: the paper's counts are decreases from each person's own pre-infusion baseline at +55 min on the ketamine day (p. 303), not ketamine-minus-placebo differences, and placebo-day means also dipped slightly at +55 (Figure 1), so the counts are not a placebo-controlled responder rate. (2) 'recover' rests on post hoc tests that were no longer significant at +90 (recognition, attention) or +120 min (free recall) in 14-15 people with no interval; 'were no longer detectably lower' is what the source shows. The limits sentence is accurate for this source; its r range (-.28 to -.41) leaves out the withdrawal-retardation correlations (-.11 and .02), which does not change the point.
claims.note: Every Malhotra number in the statement and magnitude was checked on the rendered p. 303: F(1,14) = 9.63, p = .008; F(4,52) = 4.35, p = .004; F(1,13) = 18.79, p = .001; F(1,13) = 6.25, p = .026; F(1,13) = 17.48, p = .001; F(4,52) = 7.95; F(1,13) = 8.92, p = .01; F(1,13) = 18.78; F(4,56) = 2.71, p = .05; F(1,14) = 8.79, p = .01; 13 of 15, 9 of 14, 9 of 15; n = 15 (14 for recognition, p. 302). All as printed. Recomputed p values agree (attention interaction F(4,56) = 2.71 gives p = .039 uncorrected; printed .05 is presumably after the Greenhouse-Geisser correction the methods name). Timing: +90 and +120 are 30 and 60 min after the 1-h infusion ended (Figure 1 legend), so recall was still lower 30 min after the end and not detectably lower 60 min after it, consistent with 'within about an hour or two'. The study condition is a bolus plus 1-h infusion with no blood levels measured.

anchors.locator: Methods › Subjects; Procedure; Cognitive and Behavioral Measures
anchors.extracted: 15 healthy volunteers (12 men, 3 women; mean age 27.9, +/- 7.1) from the NIH normal volunteer program, free of psychiatric disorder on the SADS interview and medically screened. Two double-blind test days, ketamine and saline, in randomized order at least one day apart. Study condition: bolus 0.12 mg/kg then 0.65 mg/kg over 1 hour (maximum 58 mg), described as 0.77 mg/kg/hr in total; no blood levels. Tests at -30, +10, +55, +90 and +120 min: a 12-word categorized list read at a 2-s rate, saying 'repeat' when one of 6 repeated words recurs (the attention score), free recall after a 2-min filled delay, then old/new recognition among 24 words (12 old, 12 new). One person's +55 recognition data missing on the ketamine day, so recognition analyses use 14.

Free recall: drug F(1,14) = 9.63, p = .008; time F(4,56) = 5.16, p = .005; drug x time F(4,52) = 4.35, p = .004; post hoc lower on ketamine at +55 min F(1,13) = 18.79, p = .001 and at +90 min F(1,13) = 6.25, p = .026. Figure 1 (read from the plot): ketamine about 6.7 words at baseline, about 3.2 at +55 against about 6.3 on placebo, about 5.3 against 6.9 at +90, and about 5.8 against 6.0 at +120 (no asterisk at +10 or +120).

Recognition (n = 14): drug F(1,13) = 17.48, p = .001; time F(4,52) = 6.05, p = .001; drug x time F(4,52) = 7.95, p < .001; post hoc lower at +10 min F(1,13) = 8.92, p = .01 and +55 min F(1,13) = 18.78, p = .001. Figure 1: ketamine about 9.0 and 8.0 of 12 at +10 and +55 against about 11.1 and 11.4 on placebo; back at the placebo level (about 11) at +90 and +120.

Attention (repeat detection): drug F(1,14) = 9.63, p = .008 (identical to the free-recall drug effect), time F(4,56) = 5.37, p = .003, drug x time F(4,56) = 2.71, p = .05; described by the authors as less robust; post hoc lower at +55 min only, F(1,14) = 8.79, p = .01. Figure 1: about 4.2 of 6 on ketamine at +10 and +55 against about 4.9 and 5.4 on placebo, equal at +90 and +120.

Individual counts at +55 min of the ketamine infusion, as decreases from the person's own pre-infusion baseline (not differences from the placebo day): 9 of 15 lower on attention, 13 of 15 lower on free recall, 9 of 14 lower on recognition.

With attention as covariate at +55 min only, the drug effect remained for free recall F(1,12) = 6.55, printed p = 0.25 (an F of 6.55 on 1 and 12 df gives p = .025, so the printed 0.25 is a misprint), and for recognition F(1,13) = 7.05, p = .025 (recomputed p = .020). This is the only adjustment for attention, at one time point. The methods (pp. 302-303, Data Analysis, 3rd paragraph) state that covariance with BPRS scores could not be run because placebo-day BPRS scores barely varied.

Correlations of ketamine-minus-placebo changes at +55 min: free recall with BPRS total r = -.28 (p = .31), thought disorder r = -.31 (p = .26), withdrawal-retardation r = -.11 (p = .71), n = 15; recognition with BPRS total r = -.28 (p = .34), thought disorder r = -.41 (p = .14), withdrawal-retardation r = .02 (p = .96), n = 14; free recall with recognition r = .64 (p = .01). Editors' calculation (Fisher z): 95% CI for r = -.28 (n = 15) -.69 to .27, for r = -.41 (n = 14) -.77 to .15, so moderate relations are not excluded; the negative signs run in the direction of larger psychosis-score rises with larger memory falls.

The authors conclude that the memory effects were not secondary to attention, were not related to psychosis ratings, and that ketamine has direct effects on free recall and recognition, resting on the one covariance analysis and the non-significant correlations above; no blinding check and no confidence interval for any cognitive measure are reported anywhere in the paper.

claims.overstatement: None for the Malhotra sentence. Two editorial inferences in it are not printed in the paper: the 'SD' label on the item values (the paper does not say SD or SEM; the printed t values are consistent only with SDs for n = 15, e.g. 2.9 +/- 1.1 against 1.0 gives t of about 6.7 if SD, printed 6.42) and the 'floor of 3' (derivable: each factor has three items, each scored from 1, and placebo means are 3.0 +/- 0.0). The opening sentence's 'pass within minutes to a couple of hours' is only partly shown here: BPRS was rated last at +90 min (30 min after the end), when the total was 21.5 against 18.7, not flagged as significant; later ratings were not made.
claims.note: All Malhotra numbers checked on the rendered Table 1 (p. 304) and text (pp. 303-304): 19.3 (0.4), 27.5 (1.6), 21.5 (1.4); placebo 19.1 (0.7), 18.7 (0.4), 18.7 (0.3); thought disorder 3.0 to 6.3 (0.6); withdrawal-retardation 3.3 to 6.6 (0.6); hallucinations item 1.2 +/- 0.5 against 1.0 +/- 0.0, t = 1.38, p = 0.190 (recomputed two-sided p with 14 df = .189). All as printed. The BPRS ANOVAs report error df of 81-82 (F(1,82) = 24.20, F(2,81) = 10.37), impossible for 15 people tested twice in a repeated-measures model; the tests look as if observations were treated as independent, so the BPRS p values are likely too small, though the +55 differences are large.

anchors.extracted: BPRS (18 items), mean +/- SEM, n = 15, at -30, +55 and +90 min: total ketamine 19.3 +/- 0.4, 27.5 +/- 1.6 (p < .001 against placebo), 21.5 +/- 1.4; placebo 19.1 +/- 0.7, 18.7 +/- 0.4, 18.7 +/- 0.3; drug x time F (df 2,81) 10.4, p < .001. Thought disorder ketamine 3.0 +/- 0.0, 6.3 +/- 0.6, 3.5 +/- 0.2, placebo 3.0 throughout, F 24.9, p < .001. Withdrawal-retardation ketamine 3.3 +/- 0.1, 6.6 +/- 0.6, 4.6 +/- 0.5, placebo 3.3, 3.5, 3.5, F 8.1, p = .001. Hostility-suspiciousness ketamine 3.3, 3.5, 3.3 against placebo 3.1, F 0.1, p = .90. Anxiety-depression 3.5, 3.9, 3.1 against 3.3, 3.1, 3.0, F 2.3, p = .10. Only the +55 values carry the p < .001 mark.

anchors.locator: Results, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs (3rd continues at top of p. 304)
anchors.extracted: BPRS total drug F(1,82) = 24.20, time F(2,82) = 9.00, drug x time F(2,81) = 10.37, all p < .001; thought disorder interaction F(2,81) = 24.99; withdrawal-retardation interaction F(2,81) = 8.12; anxiety-depression drug effect only (F(1,82) = 7.51, p = .007); hostility-suspiciousness no effect. 13 of 15 rose on thought disorder, 14 of 15 on withdrawal-retardation, 6 of 15 on anxiety-depression, 1 of 15 on hostility-suspiciousness. Items at +55 min: conceptual disorganization 2.9 +/- 1.1 against 1.0 +/- 0.0 (t = 6.42), unusual thought content 2.2 +/- 1.1 against 1.0 +/- 0.0 (t = 4.29), hallucinations 1.2 +/- 0.5 against 1.0 +/- 0.0 (t = 1.38, p = 0.190, not different), emotional withdrawal 2.1 against 1.2 (t = 3.67), motor retardation 2.3 against 1.2 (t = 5.91), blunted affect 2.2 against 1.1 (t = 4.94).

The authors state that ketamine did not commonly induce hallucinations or paranoid delusions in these healthy volunteers, while producing positive-type (thought disorganization, bizarre content, perceptual distortions) and negative-type (restricted affect, withdrawal-retardation) features; the syndrome is called similar but not identical to schizophrenia.

anchors.extracted: Double-blind, randomized order, saline on the other test day at least one day apart; bolus 0.12 mg/kg plus 0.65 mg/kg over 1 h (study condition). BPRS rated only at -30, +55 and +90 min, so nothing after 30 min post-infusion; no blinding check reported.

Correct 'Nine of the 15 scored lower on ketamine at 55 minutes' to 'Nine of the 15 showed a decrease in attention from their own baseline at 55 minutes of the ketamine infusion' (the paper's wording for this count is explicitly 'from baseline').

F1,12=6.55 (printed p=0.25; recomputed p=.025) and F1,13=7.05, p=.025 (recomputed .020) confirmed on p. 304. Locator nit: it is the first paragraph that starts on p. 304 (the page opens with the end of the item-level paragraph from p. 303), i.e. Results 4th paragraph overall.
Table 1 and p. 303 values confirmed; 27.5-18 = 9.5 and 27.5-19.3 = 8.2 recompute.

Confirmed on Table 1 and pp. 303-304. Minor: for the withdrawal-retardation interaction the text prints p < .001 and Table 1 prints .001; the card uses the table's value. The 13/14/6/1 of 15 counts are increases from baseline (p. 303), as the card's note says ('a rise').

All item means, t values and p values confirmed on pp. 303-304. The paper does not say whether the item +/- values are SD or SEM; the card's 'SD' label is an inference, consistent with the printed t values for n = 15 (e.g. (2.9-1.0)/(1.1/sqrt 15) = 6.7 against printed 6.42), and could be marked as the editors' reading.
All nine correlations and p values confirmed on p. 304 and Figure 2; editors' intervals recompute (-.69 to .27; -.77 to .15).

Consistent with Figure 1 (p. 303; +90 and +120 are 30 and 60 min post-infusion per the legend) and Table 1 +90 column. Free recall was still significantly lower at +90 (F1,13=6.25, p=.026), which 'closing on it' covers.

reporting_issues.note: Same finding in my blind reading (p. 304; F1,12=6.55 gives p=.025).
Error df 81-82 for 15 people in a two-day, three-time-point design; found independently.
Identical F(1,14)=9.63, p=.008 printed for free recall and attention drug effects, p. 303.
The statistics themselves are on p. 303 (the recognition exclusion is explained on p. 302).
Figure 1 recognition axis runs 6 to 12; the methods describe 24 old/new judgments.
Substance confirmed. Table 1 values are mean +/- SEM (footnote b), so 'hostility 3.1, SD 0.1' should read SEM 0.1 (the SD would be about 0.4 for n = 15); 3.0 +/- 0.0 is zero either way.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall high agreed, carried by domain 4 (clinician-rated BPRS in a condition that was probably recognizable, no blinding check). For domain 2, RoB 2's signalling questions give 'some concerns' for awareness alone unless deviations arose from it; 'high' there is stricter than the tool, but it does not change the overall judgment.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: 'direct effects' and 'not related' from one covariance analysis at +55 and null correlations in 14-15 people; 'brief psychosis' with the hallucinations item unchanged and hostility-suspiciousness unchanged (F 0.1, p .90), which the authors themselves concede in Discussion paragraph 5 (p. 305).

missed: The individual 'n of N' counts for attention, recall and recognition (p. 303) are decreases from each person's own pre-infusion baseline on the ketamine day, not ketamine-versus-placebo differences; placebo-day means also dipped at +10 and +55 (Figure 1), so they overstate drug responders. This affects key findings 0-2 and the claim cl_ket_acute_memory_attention.

The free-recall drug x time interaction recomputes as p = .004 on (4,52) df; the attention interaction F(4,56) = 2.71 recomputes as p = .039 uncorrected against the printed .05 (presumably Greenhouse-Geisser), so the attention effect is the least secure of the three and borderline after correction.

Hostility-suspiciousness did not change (F 0.1, p .90; only 1 of 15 rose), which with the unchanged hallucinations item bears directly on any statement that ketamine produced paranoid or hallucinatory symptoms in this sample; the card has the numbers but no key finding says it.
